_about: The pattern registry. This is the dimension the play profile counts on.
`kind` is a decision category and there are ten of them. It says what sort of
decision was being made. It cannot be the thing a habit list counts, because
every game contains removal-timing decisions, so kind occurrences accumulate
with games played rather than with mistakes made. A `pattern_id` names the
recurring behaviour itself, and that is what a profile line reports.
An unknown pattern_id is rejected rather than counted, same discipline as
mtg_stats.ARCHETYPE_ALIASES. Adding a pattern is a deliberate act: put it
here, and nowhere else. A habit spelled two ways splits into two habits and
`polarity` is the declared shape of the pattern, and it is documentation
rather than a verdict. Classification comes from the grade mix in the ledger.
Where the two disagree the profile says so, because a pattern declared a leak
that keeps grading correct is either mislabelled here or misgraded there, and

removal-engine-on-sight.label: Kills the engine creature on sight, tax and all
removal-engine-on-sight.description: Spends the answer immediately on the card the opponent's deck is built around, accepting a ward or protection cost to do it.

removal-spent-on-present-target.label: Spends removal on the target in front of him
removal-spent-on-present-target.description: Uses the answer on the only legal target available rather than holding it for the threat he already knows is coming.

removal-answers-the-enabler.label: Answers the enabler rather than the body
removal-answers-the-enabler.description: Points the answer at the graveyard, the accelerant or the tutor instead of the creature currently attacking.

removal-sequenced-around-protection.label: Sequences the answer around the opponent's protection
removal-sequenced-around-protection.description: Holds a counter to shield the sweeper, or jams the tutor under a protection spell already on the stack, so the answer lands where it can't be blanked.

removal-cheapest-legal-answer.label: Picks the cheapest legal answer and keeps the better one live
removal-cheapest-legal-answer.description: Chooses between two answers on cost and legality rather than reflex, leaving the more flexible card in hand for the next threat.

taps-out-into-open-mana.label: Taps out into open mana with an answer stranded in hand
taps-out-into-open-mana.description: Commits the whole turn's mana to a threat while the opponent has untapped sources and he is holding interaction he can no longer cast.

casts-flash-threat-on-own-turn.label: Casts a flash threat on his own main phase
casts-flash-threat-on-own-turn.description: Deploys a creature with flash at sorcery speed, giving up the end-step window and walking into sorcery-speed removal.

spends-turn-on-card-selection.label: Spends the turn's mana on card selection and loses the answer window
spends-turn-on-card-selection.description: Activates a loot or draw effect that eats the mana or discards the interaction, with the answer window still open.

holds-mana-acts-on-their-turn.label: Holds mana and acts on the opponent's turn
holds-mana-acts-on-their-turn.description: Passes with mana up and spends it on their turn, on the end step or on declare attackers, where the same card does more.

plays-what-the-mana-supports.label: Plays the line the tap trace actually supports
plays-what-the-mana-supports.description: Counts the real sources, including colour and stun counters, and takes the line that is castable rather than the one that looks best.

deploys-engine-on-curve.label: Deploys the engine on curve and converts it the same turn
deploys-engine-on-curve.description: Lands the payoff on schedule and starts generating value immediately instead of holding it for a safer turn.

boards-without-an-answer.label: Boards into a 60 with no answer to the card that beats him
boards-without-an-answer.description: Finishes boarding with nothing in the deck that handles the opponent's key card, usually because every answer shares a restriction.

cuts-the-narrow-answer-needed.label: Cuts the narrow answer the matchup actually needed
cuts-the-narrow-answer-needed.description: Trims a cheap conditional card because it looks situational, against a deck whose key threats sit exactly in its window.

boards-to-their-actual-plan.label: Boards to what the opponent's deck actually does
boards-to-their-actual-plan.description: Matches the swap to the opponent's real plan and curve rather than to the archetype's reputation.

cuts-the-tutor-for-the-card-brought-in.label: Cuts the tutor that finds the card he just brought in
cuts-the-tutor-for-the-card-brought-in.description: Brings in a one-of silver bullet and cuts the copies of the tutor that would have found it.

bottoms-the-live-answer.label: Bottoms the live answer and keeps the blank one
bottoms-the-live-answer.description: Puts the card that answers this matchup on the bottom and keeps one that the opponent's costs or card types make dead.

keeps-mana-that-cannot-cast-its-spells.label: Keeps a hand whose mana can't cast its own spells on curve
keeps-mana-that-cannot-cast-its-spells.description: Keeps on land count alone, where tapped lands and colourless sources mean the hand's cheapest spell is a turn or more late.

ships-the-unfunctional-seven.label: Ships the seven that cannot function
ships-the-unfunctional-seven.description: Mulligans a hand that can't cast anything, rather than keeping seven cards for their own sake.

ships-a-usable-seven.label: Ships a seven the deck could have used
ships-a-usable-seven.description: Mulligans a functional hand looking for a better one, and goes to six with less than the seven was worth.

land-drop-before-a-spell-that-counts-lan.label: Makes the land drop before a spell whose trigger counts lands
land-drop-before-a-spell-that-counts-lan.description: Plays the land first out of habit, changing the count a spell later in the turn reads. CR 305.1 allows the land after the spell resolves.

deploys-an-engine-with-nothing-to-fuel-i.label: Deploys an engine with nothing on board to fuel it
deploys-an-engine-with-nothing-to-fuel-i.description: Spends turns casting a payoff whose trigger needs a resource that isn't there, so none of the copies ever do anything.

trades-the-wrong-piece-into-the-counter.label: Trades the wrong piece into the counterspell
trades-the-wrong-piece-into-the-counter.description: Baits the counter with the cheap creature when a redundant copy in hand made the expensive one the cheaper trade.
